title: LiFi: LiDAR Generation from Multi-View Images via Geometric and Semantic Collaborative Guidance
claim: A dual-branch conditioning design with balanced guidance feeds a diffusion generator, turning multi-view inputs into a faithful output in another modality.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right; stacked input branches, central guidance panel, dashed color-coded boxes
description: A wide figure split into three dashed, color-coded panels read left to right. The left panel, blue, has two stacked branches. The top Geometry-Aware Branch takes multi-view camera images through a pretrained vision model. It produces depth and uncertainty maps, which go to a geometry-aware encoder and become structured features. The bottom Cross-View Semantic Branch takes surround-view images with a camera icon through a ViT. It adds position encoding and camera tokens, which go to a cross-view semantic encoder and become cross-view features. The middle panel, green, shows Dual-Branch Balanced CFG. Balance-scale icons with check and cross marks sit beside four rounded case pills with percentages: full-conditional 80%, geometry-only 5%, semantic-only 5%, unconditional 10%. The right panel, orange, shows the latent diffusion process. Noise and geometry features are concatenated and fed to a UNet with a transformer block. Semantic features enter the transformer block, and the CFG equation combines the cond and uncond noise predictions. Denoising yields a range image, which is projected into the generated LiDAR scene. Orange headings and noise textures catch the eye first.
caption: Overview of the LiFi framework. The framework takes real multi-view camera images as input and is capable of generating 3D LiDAR scenes with high fidelity that are consistent with the visual information. LiFi mainly comprises the following key designs: (i) geometry–semantic decoupled conditioning branches; (ii) a dual-branch balanced classifier-free guidance module; and (iii) a latent diffusion network integrated with Transformer blocks.
abstract: Generating LiDAR point clouds from multi-view camera images is a valuable task with applications in controllable data synthesis, cross-modal simulation and various perception tasks. However, most existing methods are not specifically designed for this task, and the quality of their generated LiDAR remains limited. Moreover, these methods typically focus only on semantic cues in images or generate LiDAR from a monocular camera image. In this work, we introduce LiFi (LiDAR From images), a dedicated framework for generating visually and geometrically aligned LiDAR scenes from multi-view camera images. LiFi guides the latent diffusion process through two complementary branches: geometry and semantics. The geometry branch constructs scene features from images through a reverse sampling algorithm and an uncertainty-aware geometric encoder combined with DepthAnything3, whereas the semantic branch provides high-level semantic representations via a cross-view interaction module. We further introduce a dual-branch balanced classifier-free guidance (CFG) strategy, which enhances the model's conditional generation capability while preserving the independent learning and collaborative controllability of the two branches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LiFi outperforms state-of-the-art methods in generating high-fidelity LiDAR scenes. The code will be publicly available at: https://github.com/szzhou88/LiFi.
